component.name: OmniMem
component.summary: Self-hosted semantic memory for AI agents

description.p: OmniMem gives Claude and other MCP clients a memory that lasts between sessions and projects: decisions, fixes, dead ends and the knowledge from the feeds you read, searched by meaning and kept on your own machine.

It sits in the tray and serves MCP on this computer, so Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, OpenCode, Mistral Vibe, Kiro and anything else that speaks MCP can share one memory. Its Settings item opens the settings panel in your browser, already signed in.

ul.li: Remembers decisions, bug fixes, gotchas and preferences, and recalls them by meaning rather than by keyword
Keeps a graveyard of approaches that were tried and abandoned, and warns an agent before it suggests one again
Briefs an agent at the start of a session with what the project already knows
Reads your RSS feeds and keeps what it learns, with each article's licence
Compiles what a project has learnt into skills, which you accept before they are written
Runs the embedding model on your own machine, with no account and nothing sent anywhere unless you add a Claude API key

description.p: The tray icon needs a desktop that shows them. On GNOME that means the AppIndicator extension; without it OmniMem opens the settings panel instead and says so.

screenshot.caption: Every memory, by namespace, state and project
Search by meaning, as an agent's recall does
A memory with its lesson, its breakthrough and what was abandoned on the way
The graveyard of approaches that didn't work

description.p: A contradiction whose other memory no longer exists can be cleared.
The contradiction scan sees new memories on a full store, a forget takes the recall log entries that found the memory, and a person can settle a contradiction no scan linked.
OmniMem records whether it believes a memory, not only whether it shows it: each memory has a trust, and recall, the briefing and skill compiles act on it.
